title: SDK compact kitchen-sink quickref
body:
Purpose: condensate the most common onboarding snippets, preflight checks, and edge-case recipes into a single-page kitchen-sink quick reference. This is intentionally informal — drop into a new project, copy the section you need, and iterate. Goal is to reduce first-10-minutes friction and provide deterministic telemetry/CI hooks for SDK teams and Solutions Eng.

Who this is for: new SDK integrators, onboarding engineers, SEs running demos, and internal Docs authors who need canonical copy for quickstarts.

Top-level sections (jump to what you need):
- Quick start (Node + Python minimal)
- First-commit preflight checklist (scripts + git hooks)
- Local dev (hermetic mode and stub runner)
- Telemetry events + minimal instrumentation contract
- Smoke tests and gating for PRs
- Common failure modes + quick remediation
- Tiny rollout / canary pattern for SDK changes
- TODOs & followups (actionable next steps)

QUICK START (copy+pasta)
1) Node (no-friction):
  - npm init -y
  - npm i @redwood/sdk
  - index.js (minimal):

    const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk');
    const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });

    async function run() {
      const r = await client.text.generate({ model: 'open-v1', prompt: 'Write a haiku about coffee' });
      console.log(r.text);
    }
    run().catch(console.error);

  - Run: REDWOOD_API_KEY=pk_test_... node index.js

2) Python (minimal):
  - pip install redwood-sdk
  - app.py example:

    from redwood import Redwood
    c = Redwood(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
    print(c.text.generate(model='open-v1', prompt='Summarize: memos are life') )

FIRST-COMMIT PREFLIGHT CHECKLIST (automate these in CI)
- Code style: run linter + fix formatting (npm run format / pre-commit format hook)
- Dependency pinning: ensure package manager lockfile present
- Example smoke: run minimal sample (Node/Python) and assert 200-ish latency < 3s in CI short-run
- Telemetry: increment sdk_version in package and emit SDK_INIT event locally
- Tests: basic unit tests included and passing

Sample package.json snippets:
  "scripts": {
    "start": "node index.js",
    "smoke": "node tests/smoke.js",
    "precommit": "npm run lint && npm run test:unit"
  }

Git hook (pre-commit) example (hooks/pre-commit):
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  set -e
  npm run lint
  npm run test:unit
  npm run smoke || { echo 'Smoke failed - fix before commit'; exit 1; }

LOCAL DEV MODE (hermetic + stub runner)
- Run a local stub server to avoid real API calls in rapid iteration. Use the lightweight stub included in SDK repo (scripts/stub-runner).
- ENV permutation: REDWOOD_LOCAL_STUB=true REDWOOD_API_KEY=stub
- Example quickflow: start stub in background, run sample app, iterate prompts. The stub supports canned responses and latency emulation (--latency-ms).

TELEMETRY CONTRACT (minimal, back-compatible)
For CI + playgrounds we require emitting three minimal events (plain JSON lines to stdout or a configurable collector):
- SDK_INIT: {sdk_name, sdk_version, language, start_time}
- SAMPLE_CALL: {endpoint, model, prompt_length, response_tokens, latency_ms}
- ERROR: {error_code, error_message, stack, user_facing}

Instrumentation tips:
- Keep payloads small. Use short string keys.
- Emit SAMPLE_CALL for every call in smoke tests only (not end-user production by default).
- Telemetry naming: redwood.sdk.init, redwood.sdk.call, redwood.sdk.error

SMOKE TESTS (fast, deterministic)
- tests/smoke.js (Node): boot with local stub, run one text.generate and assert response structure has text and tokens > 0
- CI: run smoke with --ci flag to disable retries and fail fast
- Time budgets: set smoke test timeout to 10s

Sample smoke assertion (pseudocode):
  res = client.text.generate({prompt:'x'})
  assert res.text && typeof res.text === 'string'
  assert res.tokens_count >= 1

COMMON FAILURE MODES + REMEDIES
- Network flakiness: enable short retries (3x) in SDK with exponential backoff default 300ms->600ms
- Auth errors: common cause — missing env var or key rotated. Add helpful message: "No REDWOOD_API_KEY set. Get one from Console -> API keys"
- Unexpected schema: ensure SDK validates response shape before returning. Add debug flag REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG to log raw payloads.
- Latency regressions: add per-route counters and alerts; add a local 'simulate-lag' flag for reproducibility.

TINY ROLLOUT / CANARY FOR SDK CHANGES
- Publish new SDK minor/patch to internal registry with tag canary-<sha> (npm dist-tag)
- Open a customer-sim PR that switches registry to canary tag and runs the smoke suite in CI
- Monitor SAMPLE_CALL error rate and median latency for 24 hours
- If error_rate > 1% or median latency increases > 30% rollback tag

EXAMPLE: canary promotion process
1) publish: npm publish --tag canary-<sha>
2) PR uses package@canary-<sha>, runs smoke suite
3) After approvals and metrics pass, promote to latest: npm dist-tag add package@<version> latest

UX COPY: helpful error messages
- For API quota: "Quota exceeded for key X. Check Console -> Billing or request higher quota via Support." 
- For model fallback: "Falling back to small-latency model (open-compact). See console for details."

NOTES FOR DOC AUTHORS (how to turn this into a short quickstart page)
- Keep the page under 500 words: 3 commands + 1 snippet per language + a 3-line troubleshooting section.
- Embed the telemtry contract as a small code block for 'advanced integration' only.
- Provide a downloadable zip that contains index.js, app.py, package.json, and hooks/pre-commit

OPEN ITEMS / TODOs (actionable)
- [ ] Add Ruby and Go minimal snippets (owner: Owen Li)
- [ ] Create a public minimal-smoke harness in GH actions (owner: Maya) - link JIRA: DX-212
- [ ] Wire the SDK_INIT event to oss telemetry collector (privacy review) (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Small diagram for canary flow for docs site (owner: Diego)

Context/links: link this to internal Confluence starter (linked above), GH starter repo, and JIRA DX-212 for CI work. Use this doc as canonical quickref; when converting to the site keep examples verbatim.

Handy copy for READMEs:
"Get started in <2 minutes: install the SDK, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, run npm start or python app.py. For CI use tests/smoke.sh with REDWOOD_LOCAL_STUB=true to validate changes without hitting production."

Slack anchors / common phrases to search when debugging:
- redwood-sdk-init
- smoke-suite
- canary-dist-tag

If you take anything from here: please add a short note to the top of this file with date & what you changed so we keep it as a living scratchpad.
